stance_basis: letter states regulations appear adequate if properly enforced, while noting no direct application to Rhode Island
summary: Daniel W. Varin, Chief of Statewide Planning for Rhode Island's Department of Administration, submitted a brief letter acknowledging that the proposed ORV regulations have no direct application to Rhode Island since there are no Department of the Interior lands in the state. He nonetheless offered a conditional endorsement, stating the regulations appear adequate to control ORV activity provided they are properly enforced.
complaint_summary: Varin notes the proposed ORV regulations have no direct application to Rhode Island due to the absence of Department of the Interior lands in the state, but conditionally endorses them as adequate if properly enforced.

statement.text:
In response to your letter of June 1, 1972 (received June 15), we have reviewed the draft environmental impact statement prepared by your office on implementation of Executive Order Number 11644, pertaining to the use of off-road vehicles on public lands. This review involved those parties believed to be interested in this proposal.
The proposed regulations do not have direct application to Rhode Island, since there are no Department of the Interior lands located in this state. However, they appear to be adequate to control this activity if they are properly enforced.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on this statement.
Yours yery truly,
Daniel W. Varin
Chief, Statewide Planning
